### Line chart
Trends over time drawn from a data table, with a tooltip, a legend and a sparkline size.

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `auto-init`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Public JavaScript exports: `LineChart`. See the [API index](../references/api-index.md).

Example: Monthly revenue against last year and a target is a line chart with three series. The same figures for twenty regions are a data table.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Support: Smooth monotone lines drawn from a figure's data table, with area, stacked, fade and sparkline modifiers, dashed series, gaps, a fixed y range, x labels, round y axis labels with .axis, a legend, and a pointer and keyboard tooltip.

Web adaptation: The <table> stays in the page as the text alternative and the no-JavaScript fallback; the SVG is aria-hidden and the plot is one Tab stop with a polite live tooltip.

Full parity remains unassessed. Review provenance and specification links: [capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#line-chart).

#### Contract

A `<figure class="line-chart">` holds a `<figcaption>` and a `<table>`. The first column labels the x axis; each further column is a series named by its header cell. `AutoInit()` draws the table as smooth SVG lines with x labels, a legend when there is more than one series, and a cursor and tooltip that follow the pointer. The table stays in the page, visually hidden, as the chart's text alternative; without JavaScript it shows instead of the chart.

#### Syntax

```html
<figure class="line-chart fade">
  <figcaption>Monthly revenue, 2026</figcaption>
  <table>
    <thead>
      <tr><th>Month</th><th>Revenue</th><th class="dashed">Target</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><th>Jan</th><td>$4,400</td><td>$5,200</td></tr>
      <tr><th>Feb</th><td>$3,400</td><td>$5,400</td></tr>
      <tr><th>Mar</th><td>$3,700</td><td>$5,100</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</figure>
```

#### Also documented

The Line chart section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Tokens.

#### Rules

- `line-chart-is-a-figure-with-a-table`: Write .line-chart as a <figure> holding a <table> of the data. The drawn chart is hidden from assistive technology, so the table is all a screen reader reads, and it is what shows without JavaScript.
- `line-chart-has-a-caption`: Name a .line-chart with a <figcaption>. It names the focusable plot as well as the figure; hide it with .visually-hidden when nearby text already names the chart.
